thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in preproc-service across us-west-2 (streaming routes). Auto-pager sent to @emma (oncall). :rotating_light:

emma (oncall): seeing it, joining. p95 up ~200ms -> 450ms, p99 jumped from 2s -> 9.2s on streaming endpoints. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/explore/latency?service=preproc-service&env=prod

emma (oncall): initial check - CPU on preproc workers spiking on tokenizer process, queue depth on preproc-queue is 4x usual. file descriptors look fine.

raj (infra): I'm pulling recent deploys. Last deploy to preproc-service was 2024-08-15 03:10 UTC (commit abc123) - that changed prompt-template expansion engine and added JSON-mode path optimizations.

sasha (eng-runtime): interesting — template expansion change can blow up when tool schemas are large. Are we seeing many JSON-mode requests?

emma (oncall): yes, incoming traffic flagged ~18% JSON-mode enablement in the last 5m (normally 4%). Template+tool-schema combos causing heavy parse/expand.

kevin (sre): capturing traces. p99 traces show long time spent in preproc::template_render (avg 6.8s for top traces), tokenization itself is ~400-600ms but render->tokenize handoff is delayed due to GC + large intermediate strings.

maria (cs): quick heads up — cs started getting customer complaints about slow streaming and truncated replies on apps with tool-integration. Customers reported mainly those using JSON-mode.

emma (oncall): mitigation proposal: 1) turn off JSON-mode feature-flag for streaming routes 2) throttle template expansion / add 2s server-side cap 3) scale preproc workers + restart a subset to clear memory pressure. Anyone object?

raj (infra): scaling now: +6 preproc pods (type c5-gpu-preproc), expected to join in ~80s. Applying FF toggle now to staging then prod.

deploy-bot: feature-flag toggle applied: feature.json_mode_streaming -> OFF (prod). Rollout to 100% in 15s.

emma (oncall): applying temporary request cap for template expansion via nginx header limit: X-Template-Expand-Limit=2000 chars. Pushing change to edge config.

sasha (eng-runtime): also opening a fast rollback PR for the expansion heuristic in commit abc123. If FF toggle causes regressions, we should roll that code back.

kevin (sre): monitoring queues and tail latencies. After FF toggle and scale: p95 down from 450ms -> 220ms; p99 currently 1.8s and trending down. queue depth halved.

emma (oncall): streaming stalls still reported for some long-running sessions (tail). We think this is prefix cache misses combined with large schema expansions. Plan: enable prefix cache warmup for high-volume routes and drop JSON-mode for those sessions.

maria (cs): notifying affected customers: two enterprise tenants had degraded streaming for ~6 minutes. They want incident summary and if messages were lost. Any data loss?

sasha (eng-runtime): no data loss. Responses were delayed; some streaming chunks arrived late but full responses eventually delivered except a handful of sessions where clients timed out. We'll prepare list of request IDs.

emma (oncall): capturing request IDs for timed-out clients: see logs sample below.

emma (oncall): ```
[2024-08-15T03:12:21Z] preproc-service pid=8123 req_id=req_7f3a token_count=0 route=stream.json_mode tool_schema_size=3487 status=timeout client_timeout=true
[2024-08-15T03:13:02Z] preproc-service pid=8127 req_id=req_7f8b token_count=12 route=stream.json_mode status=delivered latency=8.9s
```

raj (infra): infra note: disk I/O for redis cache looked fine. CPU + JS VM memory pressure on template renderer was main bottleneck. Scaling helped but code fix needed.

sasha (eng-runtime): short-term patch: limit tool-schema depth during expansion (fast fail and fall back to compact schema). I'll push a hotfix to the template renderer and can ship within ~20min, then canary to 10% traffic.

emma (oncall): sounds good. Can you add a guard that forces non-streaming fallback when expansion time > 1.5s? That would prevent stalls.

sasha (eng-runtime): yep adding timeout and fallback to pre-serialized template. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/preproc/pulls/4823

kevin (sre): after toggle + scaling, customer complaints dropped. p99 at 1.2s and p95 at 180ms at last check. We'll keep monitoring next 30m.

maria (cs): prepping customer comms draft: short explanation + apology + mitigation steps + ETA for full fix. Will share with oncall after we confirm hotfix.

emma (oncall): handoff plan: I'll monitor for 15 more mins then hand to @raj for night. If p99 stays <1.5s and no new timeouts, we can resolve. Otherwise escalate.

raj (infra): noted. I'll own rollback path if the FF toggle creates regressions, and confirm autoscale metrics.

sasha (eng-runtime): hotfix merged to canary (10%) now. Observing canary traces. If green in 10m, rollout to 50%.

deploy-bot: canary rollout: preproc-hotfix -> 10% -> ok

kevin (sre): canary looks clean, no regressions, p99 for canary at 720ms. Rolling to 50% over 2m.

emma (oncall): thanks team. creating incident postmortem stub with notes: cause = prompt-template expansion + JSON-mode surge + commit abc123 heuristic change; mitigations = FF toggle, scale up, hotfix to renderer, prefix cache warmup; customer impact = streaming stalls for subset of sessions, 2 enterprise tenants affected, duration ~8min peak, p99 SLO breach observed.

emma (oncall): handing off to @raj for continued monitoring and follow-through on postmortem. If anyone needs to add details, append below. :white_check_mark:

raj (infra): taking over. I'll follow up with deploy logs, exact request ids, and coordinate CS postmortem. Closing pager for @emma.

incident-bot: NOTE: pager cleared at 2024-08-15T03:20:30Z by emma (oncall).
